_doc: Each candidate's provenance and, for planted ones, the defect class (D-11) and the outcome the round must reach. expect: survive | discard-screen | discard-question | flag (survives the automated stages but is shown as strictly weaker or stronger than another survivor, for the signers). planted candidates pass if they end outside the main cluster (discarded, or flagged); correct ones pass if they end in it. 'expect_changed' records an expectation revised after a run, with the reason, so the revision is visible rather than silent.

alt-closed.author: human
alt-closed.note: closed interval; equivalent because squares are never prime, but not by a small tactic
alt-closed.expect_changed: 2026-10-09 after the witness probes: the closed interval is equivalent to the open one only because squares are never prime. The probe judges the formula against the words ('strictly between'); asked whether a prime at 1 would count for n = 1, the proposer says no, and the closed reading goes. The faithful formulas survive, so nothing is lost.

alt-inline.author: human
alt-inline.note: primality written inline, no named helper: a test of the witness probes' own assumption
alt-inline.expect_changed: 2026-10-09 after its first run: expected to survive, it was DISCARDED by the coverage probe, a false positive. With primality inline there is no predicate for the probe to replace, so the probe asked the real claim. Fixed by a format rule (a candidate names each concept the words use as its own predicate, or is returned to its author), not by changing what the probe concludes.
